props.note: Upright main hull with attached bow, missing stern and empty main-battery barbettes, following the 2001 expedition photographs (H.M.S. Hood Association). Published overall vessel length 251 m and beam 36 m set the build envelope; 15 m height and heading 20 degrees are build choices. The model snaps to terrain at the published expedition vicinity, about 4,218.5 m here, with an unresolved ~570 m difference from the real wreck depth. Do not lower the hull beneath unchanged terrain. See sources.md.

Four detached main-battery turret forms in a build scatter. The real turrets fell out during capsizing; public reports do not publish individual positions. This scatter sits upslope of the hull on the same supported terrain as before; its 50 m footprint and heading are gameplay choices. See the 2001 expedition account and sources.md.

Hull plating, frames and pipes around the torn aft end, where the stern broke away (kbismarck.com wreck summary; the stern itself has never been found). Centred ~130 m astern of the hull (bearing 200 deg from the hull fix, i.e. off the torn end for heading 20). Position, radius and piece counts are illustrative.

The underwater landslide the hull set off as it hit the seamount flank and slid down it (Ballard 1989 survey; docs/research/sites.md: 'build a scrape, small slide blocks'). Sediment blocks and edge berms in an ellipse 400 m long and 90 m wide (dimensions_m = [half-length, half-width, height] for this kit), laid from the hull up-slope toward the turret area (bearing 82 deg). The coarse terrain does not resolve the real scar; its length, width and course here are a reconstruction.
